dedupe_keys.name: transfer learning strategies for solar power forecasting under data scarcity

description: Elissaios Sarmas and colleagues publish this resource through Zenodo. The implemented model compares three transfer-learning strategies for stacked LSTM forecasting against a conventional non-transfer model and smart persistence. It forecasts hourly production at six solar plants and examines weight initialisation and feature-extraction/freezing strategies. With one year of training data, the source reports 12.6 percent RMSE improvement and 16.3 percent forecast-skill improvement; the gap increases in the reported three-month setting. These are study-specific relative results, not guaranteed performance on new plants. The model supports solar-production forecasting and associated energy balancing. No open trained weights or executable source distribution are established by the publication metadata. Native metadata gives open access and the licence label cc-by-4.0. These terms describe the deposit; a paper licence does not establish a software licence. Coverage is limited to the stated sites, model settings and application examples. Only descriptive metadata and file descriptors were inspected. Linked data, code and document bodies were not opened.
